units.text: EXT. SALT FLATS - MIDDAY
A white, cracked desert under a merciless sun.
Heat shimmers off the ground.
In the distance, an overturned jeep lies on its roof like a dead beetle.
DOROTHY MAE PRUITT, 50s, a surveyor in a wide-brimmed hat, sits in the thin shade of the jeep.
Her sister, LORETTA PRUITT, 40s, kneels beside her with a canteen held upside down, shaking out the last drops.
Across from them stands JUDGE HARLAN CREEL, 60s, a man in a ruined linen suit, one shoe missing.
Behind him, MILO, 20s, their driver, drags a spare tire from the wreck and tries to prop it against the axle as a sunshade.
Dorothy watches Loretta tilt the canteen.
Loretta does not meet her eyes.
Harlan licks his cracked lips and takes a step toward the canteen.
Milo drops the tire with a grunt, then stands between Harlan and the sisters without seeming to decide to.
There's a well at the old mine. Four miles.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Four miles that way, or four miles you think that way?
units.name: DOROTHY

units.text: I'm not in the habit of guessing.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: You're missing a shoe, Judge.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: Harlan glances at his bare foot.
He tucks it behind the other.
She's right about the distance. I drove past it Thursday.
units.name: MILO

units.text: Thursday you drove past everything.
units.name: DOROTHY

units.text: Milo says nothing.
He picks the tire up again.
Loretta caps the empty canteen and slowly hands it to Dorothy.
Dorothy turns it in her palm, then hands it back.
Loretta puts it in her bag.
Neither speaks.
Harlan watches the trade as if it were a verdict.
If we leave now, we reach it by dusk.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: And if we wait?
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: Then we wait for a different problem.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Dorothy stands, brushes salt from her skirt.
She takes Loretta's hat and sets it on her sister's head, straightening the brim.
Four miles.
units.name: DOROTHY

units.text: She starts walking.
Loretta follows.
Harlan hesitates, then limps after them.
Milo leaves the tire behind and falls in last, eyes on the horizon.
